solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drawing of son penned by father changing hands (6)

indicatorNotes.penned by: to be penned is to be shut in a pen, so the son is enclosed by the father's letters
indicatorNotes.changing hands: hands are right and left, and changing them swaps the R for an L

blocks.note: pater, Latin for father, is old public-school slang for dad
the R (right hand) becomes L (left hand)
s = son, the genealogy abbreviation; it goes after the second letter

annotation.surface: A child's portrait is sketched by his father, who switches to drawing with his other hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' sounds like a sale or a switch of drawing hand; in crosswords R and L stand for right and left, so it swaps one letter for the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pastel is a picture drawn in pastel crayons.

entries.clue: European author admitting regrets about boat (10)

indicatorNotes.admitting: to admit is to let in, so the author lets the rest inside him
indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the regrets wrap round the boat

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American author; his letters split after PO
rues = regrets; it splits after its first letter
a tug is a small boat that tows ships

annotation.surface: A European writer confesses to some remorse over a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The containers nest: the boat goes inside the regrets first, and that whole unit then goes inside the author.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by nationality: a Portuguese person is a European.

entries.clue: Some former customers sent back out-of-date bread from Ecuador (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: some of the letters, not all, so the answer is a run inside the phrase
indicatorNotes.sent back: something sent back goes the way it came, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: the last two letters of former and first three of customers

annotation.surface: A shop's lapsed customers return stale bread they bought in Ecuador.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, not a loaf; Ecuador's old currency was replaced by the US dollar in 2000, hence out-of-date.
annotation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and the sucre was Ecuador's currency until 2000.

entries.clue: Stores penny inside of bare monument (7)

indicatorNotes.inside of: inside of means within, so the penny goes into what follows
indicatorNotes.bare: something bare has its covering stripped off, so the monument loses its outer letters

blocks.note: a memorial is a monument
MEMORIAL without its first and last letters
p = penny; it goes after the second letter

annotation.surface: Shops keep a coin tucked inside a plain memorial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inside of bare' tempts you to take the middle of BARE; instead 'inside of' places the penny and 'bare' strips the monument.
annotation.definitionFit: A plural synonym: emporia, the Latin plural of emporium, are large stores.

entries.clue: Murder in manor overseen by police officer? (8)

blocks.note: DI = Detective Inspector, with the possessive 's: the officer's
manor is British police slang for the district an officer oversees, their patch

annotation.surface: A detective-story killing in a country house, with the inspector in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Manor' reads as a stately home; in British police slang it is the district an officer works, so a manor overseen by a DI is the DI's patch. The question mark flags that playful possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to dispatch someone is to kill them.

entries.clue: Rebels once returned home bearing diamonds (5)

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned comes back the way it went, so the word reads upwards
indicatorNotes.bearing: to bear is to carry, and in a down clue the lower part carries the upper on its back

blocks.note: ice is underworld slang for diamonds
in = at home

annotation.surface: Old rebels come home with stolen diamonds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' dates the rebels: this is the British tribe that rose against Rome.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by history: Boudicca led the Iceni in revolt against Roman rule around AD 60.

entries.clue: Criticise American male cramping Charlie’s style (7)

indicatorNotes.cramping: to cramp is to squeeze into a tight space, so the American male hems Charlie in

blocks.note: to pan = to criticise harshly, as reviewers do
a = American
Charlie = C in the phonetic alphabet; the 's is only surface
he = a male

annotation.surface: A critic complains that an American man is holding back Charlie's flair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charlie's style' reads as one phrase, but only C is used and 'style' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: panache is flamboyant style.

entries.clue: Won ton and steak one splits with editor after hours (9)

indicatorNotes.splits: one splits the steak by going into the middle of it, dividing it in two
indicatorNotes.after: the editor comes after the hours, so its letters follow

blocks.note: t = ton
rump is a cut of steak; it splits after its first letter
I = one, the Roman numeral
h = hours
ed = editor

annotation.surface: A late-night Chinese meal: wonton, and a steak shared with the editor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Won ton' looks like the dumpling, wonton; split it and 'Won' is the definition while 'ton' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to triumph is to come out on top in a contest.

entries.clue: Take notice of Scottish nut on the radio (4)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: radio is only heard, never seen, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: heid is Scots for head, and nut is slang for head

annotation.surface: Listen when a Scottish madman speaks on the radio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nut' suggests a madman or something edible; here it is slang for the head, and the Scots word is heid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to heed advice is to take notice of it.

entries.clue: Fan of film clubs during endless holiday? (8)

indicatorNotes.endless: without an end, so the holiday loses its last letter

blocks.note: c = clubs, the card suit
in = during, as in 'in the night'
Easter is a holiday
the holiday minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A film buff joins cinema clubs to fill a long holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Film clubs' reads as one phrase, but 'Fan of film' is the definition and 'clubs' is the card suit.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed word: cineaste comes from French for a cinema enthusiast.

entries.clue: English church enclosed by tangled privet’s open (9)

indicatorNotes.enclosed by: enclosed means fenced in, so the English church sits inside the hedge
indicatorNotes.tangled: a tangled hedge has its twigs all mixed up, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: PRIVET rearranged, opened after its first letter
e = English
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: An English church hidden behind an overgrown hedge is open to visitors.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition 'open'; privet is a common British hedging shrub.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone receptive is open to new ideas.

entries.clue: Sound offensive when out of order (5)

indicatorNotes.out of: to be out of something is to have none of it left, so the order is taken away

blocks.note: noisome = offensive, foul-smelling
OM = Order of Merit, removed from the fifth and sixth letters

annotation.surface: A sound is offensive when it breaks the rules.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' reads as a phrase meaning unacceptable; here 'order' is the Order of Merit, a British honour, and 'out of' removes it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: noise is sound, especially unwanted sound.

entries.clue: One nude man dancing with Eric generates interest? (8,6)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancers move about and change places, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters
anagram fodder, added 'with' the rest

annotation.surface: A naked man dancing with Eric draws plenty of attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks like curiosity about the naked dancer; it is interest on money, earned without working, and the question mark flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: interest on savings is income you did no work for.

entries.clue: Really hot time visiting wild Lewes band (10)

indicatorNotes.visiting: a visitor goes inside, so the time stays within the rearranged town
indicatorNotes.wild: something wild is out of control, so the town's letters run riot

blocks.note: LEWES rearranged, opened before its last letter
t = time
a ring is a band, as round a finger

annotation.surface: A band plays a scorching set on a visit to wild Lewes.
annotation.walkthrough: Lewes is a town in East Sussex, famous for its riotous Bonfire Night, which makes 'wild' fit the surface; 'band' is a ring, not a group of musicians.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sweltering means oppressively, really hot.

entries.clue: Wrongful trading involves taking extreme positions (5)

indicatorNotes.involves: to involve is to include, so the phrase holds the answer within it

blocks.note: the last two letters of the first word and first three of the second

annotation.surface: Illegal trading means taking wild risks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a business report on market positions, which hides the join across the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective: ultra describes someone who holds extreme views.

entries.clue: Island Royal Engineers Group erected fair (9)

indicatorNotes.erected: something erected is stood upright, so in a down clue the string reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: Elba, Napoleon's island of exile
RE = Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a lot is a group, as in 'that lot'

annotation.surface: Army engineers put up a fair on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair' in the surface is a funfair; as the definition it means passable.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fair and tolerable both mean passable, neither good nor bad.

entries.clue: Screen display of pig stuffed with 50 fish hearts (5,4)

indicatorNotes.stuffed with: a stuffed pig has filling packed inside it, so the other letters go into the pig

blocks.note: a sow is a female pig; it opens after its first letter
L = 50 in Roman numerals
ides are fish, the plural of ide
h = hearts, the card suit

annotation.surface: A cookery programme shows a pig stuffed with fifty fish hearts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fish hearts' reads as offal, but it is two pieces: ides (the ide is a freshwater fish) and the card suit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a slide show is a sequence of images displayed on a screen.

entries.clue: Sloth edges along lacking cover on headland (8)

indicatorNotes.lacking cover: without its cover, the top layer, so in a down clue the first letter goes
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so the headland comes below

blocks.note: to sidle is to edge along
the first letter removed
a ness is a headland, as in Dungeness and Sheerness

annotation.surface: A sloth creeps along a headland without shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures the animal; the definition is the deadly sin of sloth.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sloth is laziness.

entries.clue: Really short fat hawk picked up green power unit (5,4)

indicatorNotes.short: short means cut off, so the fat loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.picked up: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: so = really, as in 'so good'
lard is pig fat
the fat without its last letter
to hawk goods is to sell them

annotation.surface: A very small, plump hawk is spotted by a birdwatcher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' is the verb, to peddle goods, not the bird; 'green' means environmentally friendly.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a renewable device that turns sunlight into electricity, so a green unit of power.

entries.clue: African managed to carry Rod (7)

indicatorNotes.to carry: to carry is to hold, so the word for managed holds the rod inside it

blocks.note: ran = managed, as in ran a business; it opens after its first letter
a wand is a rod

annotation.surface: An African manages to carry his friend Rod.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Rod look like a man's name; it is just a rod.
annotation.definitionFit: A nationality: someone from Rwanda is an African.

entries.clue: Ideal way of working came first in review (5)

indicatorNotes.in review: to review is to look back over, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: MO = modus operandi, a way of working
led = came first, was in front

annotation.surface: An appraisal finds the ideal working method came out on top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Review' reads as an appraisal; it means looking back.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective sense: something held up as an example to copy, like a model citizen, is perfect of its kind.

entries.clue: As lead might unfortunately be in factory or in theatre (7)

annotation.definition: As lead might unfortunately be in factory or in theatre

blocks.clueFragment: As lead might unfortunately be in factory
blocks.note: lead the metal, poured badly into a mould in a foundry
the lead the star role, given to the wrong actor

annotation.surface: Things can go wrong with the lead, whether in a foundry or on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: Lead is both the metal, badly poured into a mould in a factory, and the lead actor, given the wrong part in a theatre.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses of cast meet: metal cast badly, or an actor cast in an unsuitable role.

entries.clue: Rest book on object held by snake expert (9,5)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, on means next to, so the pieces follow in order
indicatorNotes.held by: to be held is to be gripped inside, so the object goes within the snake

blocks.note: b = book
re = on, concerning
an asp is a venomous snake; it opens after its first letter
a thing is an object
an ace is an expert

annotation.surface: Put the book down on something a snake handler is holding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snake expert' reads as a herpetologist, but it is two separate pieces, and the snake does the holding.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a breathing space is a rest or pause.

entries.clue: Books in here on vacation close to Rhyl? (5)

annotation.definition: Books in here on vacation close to Rhyl?

indicatorNotes.in: the books go inside what follows
indicatorNotes.on vacation: vacation means emptying, so the word keeps only its outer letters
indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its end, so its last letter

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament, the books of the Bible
HERE emptied of its middle, split round the books
last letter of Rhyl

annotation.surface: Holidaymakers bring books to read somewhere near Rhyl.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: on holiday near Rhyl, a Welsh seaside resort, you book into one; the question mark marks it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: read straight, the clue describes where you book a room on a seaside holiday.

entries.clue: Playwright’s spirit that is drunk by patrol’s regulars (5)

indicatorNotes.drunk by: what is drunk goes inside the drinker, so the letters for 'that is' go within
indicatorNotes.regulars: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of patrol
i.e. = that is; it goes before the last letter

annotation.surface: A patrol's regular drinkers down a playwright's favourite spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like drink, which 'drunk' encourages; the playwright is Shakespeare, and this is the spirit in The Tempest.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary reference: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

entries.clue: Rock music follows compere’s introduction (4)

indicatorNotes.follows: to follow is to come after, so in a down clue the music sits below
indicatorNotes.introduction: an introduction comes at the start, so only the first letter of compere is used

blocks.note: first letter of compere
rag = ragtime music

annotation.surface: A rock band plays after the host introduces them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock music' reads as one phrase; 'Rock' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A kind of: a crag is a steep, rugged mass of rock.

entries.clue: Plunder near centre of Almedina maybe decent (5)

indicatorNotes.near: near means right beside, so the second piece sits next to the first
indicatorNotes.centre of: the centre is the middle, so the two middle letters of the town

blocks.note: to rob is to plunder
the middle two of its eight letters

annotation.surface: Looting near the old town of Almedina might be acceptable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Decent' reads as respectable; it means clothed, as in 'are you decent?', and 'maybe' admits a robe is one way of being so.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: wearing a robe is one way to be decent, meaning dressed.

entries.clue: Titanium coating very large tin and nickel conductor (9)

indicatorNotes.coating: a coating wraps round the outside, so titanium's letters go either side
indicatorNotes.and: and adds the nickel on the end

blocks.note: Ti = titanium, its chemical symbol, split to wrap round
OS = outsize, a clothing label
a can is a tin
Ni = nickel, its chemical symbol

annotation.surface: A list of metals: titanium coating tin and nickel, as in a good electrical conductor.
annotation.walkthrough: The chemistry surface makes 'conductor' look like one that carries electricity; it is the Italian orchestral conductor Arturo Toscanini.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Arturo Toscanini was one of the most famous orchestral conductors.

entries.clue: Somehow feel angry expelling a nuisance from bed? (8)

indicatorNotes.Somehow: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are put together in another order
indicatorNotes.expelling: to expel is to throw out, so the A leaves the fodder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters
the A thrown out before rearranging

annotation.surface: Someone is furious at being turfed out of bed by a pest.
annotation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not a place to sleep; these aphids plague garden plants.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: greenfly are aphids, a pest from garden beds.

entries.clue: Camp unaccompanied man crossing city (6)

indicatorNotes.crossing: to cross something is to lie across it, so the man spans the city on both sides

blocks.note: a man who goes stag goes to a party without a partner
LA = Los Angeles; it goes before the last letter

annotation.surface: A flamboyant single man walks across a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like an adjective describing the man; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A kind of: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War.
